answer: Proof-of-stake mechanisms anchor Sybil resistance within a nebula of cryptographic assets. By requiring agents to lock capital as a kernel of authority, the network mandates that every identity expansion incurs a direct financial plume of opportunity cost. An attacker must exhaust their liquid capital to provision fake identities, as the cost of validating blocks scales linearly with the stake, ensuring that malicious influence remains computationally and economically prohibitive.
